pages.title: Overview
pages.text: The Tesla Coil is the mod's only wireless power tower. It stores no power itself and never connects directly to a machine: every AC appliance (industrial fermenter, freezer, ice cream maker, juice extractor, electric steamer) depends on it to run.$(br2)The coil draws power from the side $(l)opposite its facing$(): put a Faraday Generator, a Wind Turbine Controller, or an AC/DC Converter in DC-to-AC mode against that face. Each extra coil in the chain weakens the power, so keep generators right next to the coil.

pages.title: Range
pages.text: The coil reaches 8 blocks in each of the six directions — up and down, front and back, left and right — forming a cross-shaped supply area of 48 positions.$(br2)Every working appliance inside is charged for one second at a time; machines tucked diagonally in a corner get nothing.

pages.title: Overload
pages.text: The coil settles accounts every 3 seconds: it totals the draw of every appliance in range, subtracts that from its available power, and only what is left actually gets delivered.$(br2)If the result is zero or less the coil overloads — it stops glowing and stops supplying power, and the power readout in its interface turns red. Run fewer machines at once, or hook up a stronger generator.

pages.title: Chained Coils
pages.text: If a coil has no generator attached, it tries to draw from the most efficient coil in range instead, but it only receives 80%% of that coil's output (the transfer efficiency can be changed in the config).$(br2)Every extra link in the chain loses another share of the power.

pages.title: Stay Safe
pages.text: A working coil keeps throwing sparks and shocks every creature within about 1.2 blocks, with damage scaling with its current power. Players are hurt too — do not stand next to a working coil.$(br2)Right-click to open the interface and turn on the particle display to see the 48-block supply area for yourself.

pages.title: Placement Tips
pages.text: The coil's facing decides which side it draws from: the block $(l)behind$() its facing must touch an AC generator. Once placed, right-click it with a Crowbar to rotate it — no need to break and re-place.
